definitions.definition: A made-up field that mixes theology (study of God) and physics (study of the universe) to explain everything using math and God.
definitions.example: Like using math to prove why God created the universe.

definitions.definition: A basic rule or starting point that you accept as true without proof, used to build other ideas.
definitions.example: In math, '1+1=2' is an axiom.

definitions.definition: To figure out or get a result from basic rules or evidence.
definitions.example: You derive the answer to a puzzle by using clues.

definitions.definition: The Christian message about Jesus's life, death, and resurrection, meaning 'good news.'
definitions.example: The gospel says God loves everyone and offers forgiveness.

definitions.definition: Sacred writings, like the Bible, considered holy by a religion.
definitions.example: Christians read scripture to learn about God.

definitions.definition: Something that doesn't make sense or is logically impossible.
definitions.example: Saying 'square circle' is incoherent because it can't exist.

definitions.definition: The base material or surface that something else sits on or lives in.
definitions.example: Paper is the substrate for ink in a notebook.

definitions.definition: A measure of disorder or randomness in a system; things naturally tend to get messier over time.
definitions.example: Your room gets messy on its own, but it takes work to clean it.

definitions.definition: Being locked alone in a cell with no contact with other people, used as punishment.
definitions.example: A prisoner in solitary confinement sees no one for days.

definitions.definition: An enemy or opponent, often referring to Satan in Christian belief.
definitions.example: In the Bible, the adversary tries to trick people into doing wrong.

definitions.definition: Not balanced or equal on both sides; one side has an advantage.
definitions.example: A fight between a tank and a slingshot is asymmetric.

definitions.definition: Gets worse or bigger over time, like interest on a loan.
definitions.example: A small problem compounds if you ignore it, becoming huge.

definitions.definition: When different things come together to a single point or agreement.
definitions.example: All roads converge at the city center.

definitions.definition: When everything happens exactly according to cause and effect, with no randomness.
definitions.example: A clock is deterministic: gears move in a fixed way.

definitions.definition: When things happen based on chance or probability, not fixed rules.
definitions.example: Rolling dice is probabilistic because you can't predict the exact number.

definitions.definition: Something that is everywhere or spreads through everything.
definitions.example: The internet is pervasive in modern life.

definitions.definition: The belief that God became a human being in the form of Jesus Christ.
definitions.example: Christmas celebrates the incarnation of God as a baby.

definitions.definition: Coming back to life after being dead, especially Jesus rising from the tomb.
definitions.example: Easter celebrates the resurrection of Jesus.

definitions.definition: Paths or directions that something follows over time.
definitions.example: A ball thrown in the air has a curved trajectory.

definitions.definition: The actual thing that a word or symbol points to or represents.
definitions.example: The referent of 'dog' is the real animal, not the word itself.

definitions.definition: The state of being first or most important.
definitions.example: In a race, primacy goes to the winner.

definitions.definition: A method to make data smaller by removing repeated or unnecessary parts.
definitions.example: ZIP files use a compression algorithm to shrink photos.

definitions.definition: The idea that some true statements can't be proven within a system, from Gödel's theorem.
definitions.example: In math, incompleteness means some truths are beyond proof.

definitions.definition: Going beyond normal limits or experience, often referring to God or the spiritual.
definitions.example: A beautiful sunset can feel like a moment of transcendence.

definitions.definition: Something that cannot be made simpler or broken down into smaller parts.
definitions.example: A single atom of gold is irreducible into simpler gold.

definitions.definition: The idea that watching or measuring something can change how it behaves, especially in quantum physics.
definitions.example: Checking if a light is on can change its state in some experiments.

definitions.definition: The structure or design of right and wrong built into the universe.
definitions.example: Moral architecture means the universe has rules about good and evil.

definitions.definition: When quantum particles stop acting weirdly together and start acting normal, like losing their special connection.
definitions.example: Decoherence is like two dancers losing their perfect sync.

definitions.definition: Wrongly giving credit or blame to the wrong person or thing.
definitions.example: Misattributing your success to luck when it was hard work.

definitions.definition: An event so unlikely that it's practically impossible to happen by chance.
definitions.example: Winning the lottery 100 times in a row is a statistical impossibility.

definitions.definition: Limits or rules that restrict what can be done.
definitions.example: Time and money are constraints on a project.

definitions.definition: The moment when small changes become big enough to cause a major shift.
definitions.example: Adding one more straw to a camel's back is the tipping point.

definitions.definition: Based on observation or experiment, not just theory.
definitions.example: A doctor uses empirical evidence from tests to diagnose you.
